Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at Helix asked us to confirm the liability cap carve-out language for IP claims before we sign the Order Form. Their ask: carve-out so that any indemnity for third-party IP infringement is not bound by the monetary cap and that Redwood will pursue remedy (including replacement/patch and monetary damages) — Helix specifically wants a short notice-to-defend window (30 days) and an evidence standard that allows Helix to require Redwood to defend within that notice.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept: (a) a full carve-out for IP indemnity from the liability cap, (b) a 30-day notice window, and (c) the types of evidence Helix should provide to trigger Redwood's indemnity?

If you need a copy of our internal redlines, I can share. We are targeting signature next week.

Cheers,

Maeve —

Appreciate the clarity. I'm looping in Legal (Marissa) and Contracts (Rishi) to propose narrow language that balances Helix's request with Redwood's risk appetite. High level from product/sales: Redwood is generally willing to accept an IP indemnity carve-out, but we need clear triggering evidence and a remedy ladder (e.g., right to substitute model, injunctive relief, monetary damages limited to certain categories) plus a short cure period for Redwood to remediate.

Can Legal advise on: (1) whether Redwood can accept an unlimited monetary exposure for IP claims or whether we need a sub-cap (e.g., up to 3x revenue attributable to the use); (2) a 30-day notice cadence vs. 45 days; and (3) a short list of acceptable evidence to trigger indemnity (claim letter, complaint, DMCA notice, or patent filing).

I attached Helix's redline (they said they'd share it later) — when Legal has a proposed redline, can Contracts prepare an exec summary for the sales contact to move quickly? Helix needs sign-off by 11/27.

Thanks —

Subject: RE: Order form: carve-out to cap for IP indemnity (request)

Jasmine / Rishi —

Thanks for the heads up. Attached is a short redline (redline_MSA_v3.docx) and an evidence checklist (evidence_checklist.pdf) for Helix. Key points from Legal: 

- Scope: Redwood can accept a carve-out for IP indemnity (claims by third parties alleging infringement) where Redwood has indemnity obligations for use of the model as provided (no customer modifications that create the claim).

- Monetary exposure: Legal prefers a limited exception to a single uncapped exposure. Proposed compromise: carve out IP indemnity from the general liability cap only for equitable relief and costs of defense; for monetary damages, impose a high sub-cap (we propose 3x the fees paid by Helix in the prior 12 months, minimum $250k). This preserves predictability.

- Notice & investigation: We can accept a 30-day notice-to-defend if the external claimant's complaint and supporting documents are produced promptly. Redwood needs the right to investigate and engage counsel.

- Evidence list (see attached): required: (a) full complaint or claim letter identifying the asserted IP, (b) documentation showing Helix's use of the allegedly infringing output or model invocation logs, (c) proof of ownership or chain of title (assignment/registration), and (d) if available, any prior takedown/DMCA notices. For initial triage, a claim letter + sample outputs + model invocation logs should be sufficient to trigger a preliminary defense obligation.

- Bailment / escrow: For particularly sensitive cases, propose optional escrow of disputed content or an independent escrow arrangement — we included wording to allow temporary access to invocation logs under NDA.

I'll note that completely uncapped monetary exposure is a non-starter for us in enterprise deals without senior approval. If Sales needs to accept that ask for strategic reasons, we'll escalate to GC with justification.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_MSA_v3.docx (MS Word redline), evidence_checklist.pdf (PDF)

Quick operational notes for the sales thread: 

- If Sales is OK with the proposed sub-cap (3x last-12 months fees, floor $250k) we can push that as the default compromise. 
- If Helix insists on fully uncapped monetary obligations, get a written escalation to request GC sign-off and an economic rationale (strategic value, ARR, referenceability).
- Evidence POA: the checklist attached to Marissa's redline is what Legal will accept to open a defense. For immediate triage, Helix should provide: claim letter/complaint, sample outputs (with timestamps), and model invocation logs (we'll accept hashed logs if necessary).

Operational ask: Jasmine, please confirm whether Helix can share invocation logs and whether they want Redwood to host a temporary evidence dropbox (we can provide a secure GCS folder under NDA). Also ask Helix to confirm their preferred notice window — if they can accept 45 days it buys us runway.

- Rishi

Jasmine —

Thanks, Marissa and Rishi — this is helpful. We reviewed Redwood's suggested compromise internally and Helix can accept the proposed sub-cap (3x trailing 12 months fees with $250k floor) for monetary damages. We also agree to provide the evidence set you requested: complaint/claim letter, sample outputs (we can export logs), and proof of ownership/assignment where available.

On invocation logs: Helix can export hashed invocation logs; however, we prefer Redwood host a secure evidence bucket under NDA to streamline transfers. I'll attach Helix's redline (we've also tracked a couple of small order-form edits) and share a DocuSign link for the current Order Form in a follow-up. Can you confirm Redwood's standard timeline to ingest evidence and begin defense (we'd like acknowledgement within 72 hours of receipt)?

If all good, we plan to circulate final redline + DocuSign by Monday 11/23.

Best,
